title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics + parity + version bumps (v1.35.0)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Multiple SDKs had drifted in how authentication, retry/backoff logic, and streaming ergonomics behave. This causes surprising behavior for cross-platform clients and makes it harder for users to migrate between languages. This PR unifies the surface area and runtime behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, fixes a handful of parity issues, and bumps SDK package versions to v1.35.0.

What this PR does (summary):
- Centralizes auth provider interface and token refresh behavior so all SDKs follow the same TTL and refresh-on-401 strategy.
- Implements common retry policies: idempotent vs non-idempotent defaults, exponential backoff with jitter, and max-retries config.
- Improves streaming ergonomics: Python now exposes an async generator for tokenized streaming, TypeScript adds AsyncIterable support and better types for stream events, Go adds context-aware stream cancellation and a StreamEvent enum parity.
- Parity fixes: consistent error types and codes across SDKs, unified envelope for function/tool-calling events, align default timeouts.
- Version bumps: python 1.35.0, typescript 1.35.0, go 1.35.0 - package metadata updated and changelogs generated.
- Tests: added end-to-end streaming fixtures, cross-SDK integration tests for retry scenarios, and migration docs.

Notable implementation details:
- Auth: Introduced a minimal AuthProvider interface in each SDK. Providers must implement get_token() / refresh_token() semantics; token TTL and preemptive refresh window set to 60s by default. For backwards compatibility, existing token callback adapters are supported via an adapter shim.
- Retries: RetryPolicy enum with Idempotent/NonIdempotent. Default behavior: 3 retries for idempotent requests, 1 retry for non-idempotent. Backoff: base=100ms, multiplier=2.0, jitter=uniform(0.5-1.0). All values configurable via client options.
- Streaming: Token events, delta tokens, and end-of-stream markers standardized. Python: async generator used in streaming.text_stream(); TypeScript: client.stream().[Symbol.asyncIterator]() implemented; Go: StreamEvents channel emits typed events and respects context cancellations.
- Migration: Migration guide added to SDK docs (docs/migrations/v1.35.0.md) outlining adapter usage for custom auth, opt-in for old retry behavior, and streaming ergonomics examples.

Testing and CI:
- Ran unit test suites for all three SDKs and the cross-language integration harness.
- Streaming-e2e was flaky on first CI run (race in Go stream cancellation test); fixed by adding a small synchronization barrier in the test fixture and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Files/areas touched: redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-go, docs, release metadata, changelogs.

Risks and compatibility:
- Default retry counts changed (increase for idempotent requests). This is opt-out via client options for users who depended on previous behavior.
- Auth provider surface is backward compatible via adapter; however, advanced custom providers should be validated against the new preemptive refresh window.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4521)
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests (cross-SDK) added
- [x] Docs/migration guide added
- [x] Release notes prepared
